answer: For a botanical data market, allocate one reward budget per independently inspected land parcel, not per reporting agent. Surveys of juniper and yarrow attach a parcel ID; the ledger totals every claim against that shared budget. At an unpredictable audit pulse, inspectors request fresh geolocated measurements and reject overlapping parcel registrations. A thousand aliases on one plot still share one payout. Expanding a farm requires renting more land and paying for inspections. This relies on an honest parcel registry and spot checks.
